proposal.summary: Multiple Draytek products use hardcoded encryption keys in specified firmware versions, allowing attackers to bind affected devices to attacker-controlled accounts and create/synchronize WCF and DrayDDNS licenses via the website.
proposal.affected_product: Draytek Vigor Routers firmware < 3.9.6/4.2.4; Access Points firmware < v1.4.0; Switches firmware < 2.6.7; Myvigor firmware < 2.3.2
proposal.cwe_quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys

AV.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

AC.quote: were discovered to use hardcoded encryption keys which allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

PR.quote: allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

I.quote: Attackers are then able to create WCF and DrayDDNS licenses and synchronize them from the website.

A.quote: allows attackers to bind any affected device to their own account.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Obtain an affected device or firmware image and reproduce the binding and license-creation workflow to confirm the hardcoded key and attack surface; coordinate with vendor to identify affected builds, revoke or rotate keys, and prepare firmware updates and mitigations.
